## Who we are

Sambhavam center is based in Whitefield, Bangalore in the same premises as Orange international preschool, AECS Layout. 

We work with children who need additional support to participate in classrooms, learn alongside others and navigate everyday experiences. Our work brings together language and communication, social participation, emotional regulation and learning, with the child’s agency at its centre—their ability to express preferences, make choices and influence what happens in their lives.

Our immediate focus is to help children communicate through the means they choose, develop skills that matter in their everyday lives, and find interest and enjoyment in learning. In the longer term, we work towards equipping families to understand their children’s needs and support them as those needs evolve.

We believe education and therapy should work together. Drawing on our collective education and experience in learning, child development, psychology and behaviour, we seek to understand each child from more than one perspective. We make space for children to explore, observe their interests and responses carefully, and work closely with families to connect new learning with what children already know and experience.

## What we are working towards

### Learning that matters beyond a session

We ask not only whether a child can achieve a goal during a session, but how that learning will help them in everyday life. We want children to have more ways to express themselves, participate in family and community life, develop independence and explore new interests.

This means taking time to understand each child’s communication, strengths, preferences and support needs. It also means reviewing whether the goals we choose are meaningful in the child’s own context.

### Inclusion built through shared responsibility

For us, inclusion is much more than being in the same space as other children. It means developing a sense of belonging through relationships, participation and connection with the people and environment around the child.

We work towards this through planning, discussion and collaboration with teachers and families. Supporting inclusion also means strengthening adults’ understanding of neurodiversity and their ability to respond thoughtfully. We consider what adults, activities and environments can change, rather than placing the entire responsibility for inclusion on the child or the therapist.

### Families as partners

We believe parents should have visibility into how we work and opportunities to understand, question and contribute to the process.

Our regular conversations with families help us understand children’s experiences beyond Sambhavam. Together, we review whether learning is carrying over into everyday situations, identify where further support is needed and reconsider goals when family priorities or the child’s needs change.

## How We Put This into Practice

We hold clear goals while remaining willing to question our assumptions. When an approach is not helping a child, we treat that as feedback on our practice—a reason to observe more closely, reconsider our expectations and make changes.

Our work is supported by:

- **Individualised planning:** We connect goals with the child’s current abilities, interests, everyday experiences and family priorities.
- **Careful observation and documentation:** We record what happens, look for patterns and use these observations to guide decisions.
- **Weekly team reviews:** We discuss goals, interventions and children’s learning, bringing together observations, documented information and different professional perspectives.
- **Regular parent reviews:** We explore how children are doing across settings and plan together to support learning beyond sessions.
- **Ongoing professional learning:** Programme reviews and monthly training give therapists opportunities to deepen their understanding, question familiar approaches and strengthen their practice.

Our aim is to make the time children spend at Sambhavam purposeful, engaging and responsive—supporting meaningful progress while leaving room for exploration and discovery.
